title: HTML5 Elements and APIs Overview
description: Explore new HTML5 elements and APIs introduced for enhanced functionality and interactivity.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the <canvas> element in HTML5?
quiz.explanation: <canvas> provides a drawable region controlled with JavaScript.

quiz.question: Which HTML5 element represents a progress bar?
What is the difference between <meter> and <progress> elements?
options: <meter> shows a scalar measurement within a known range, <progress> shows task progress
They both serve the same purpose
<meter> is for audio, <progress> is for video
quiz.correctAnswer: <meter> shows a scalar measurement within a known range, <progress> shows task progress
quiz.explanation: <meter> can indicate values like disk usage, while <progress> indicates task completion.

quiz.question: Which elements provide a built-in way to show and hide content interactively?
quiz.explanation: <details> creates a collapsible section controlled by <summary>.

quiz.question: Which API allows you to draw 2D graphics on a webpage?
quiz.explanation: Canvas API is used with the <canvas> element for drawing.

quiz.question: What attribute of <progress> indicates the maximum value?
quiz.explanation: 'max' sets the maximum value for the progress bar.

quiz.question: Can the <details> element be used without a <summary> element?
quiz.explanation: <summary> is optional but recommended for accessibility.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the <meter> element?
options: Display numeric scalar measurements within a range
quiz.correctAnswer: Display numeric scalar measurements within a range
quiz.explanation: <meter> is for measurements like disk space, temperature, etc.
